answer: Each agent must stake a scarce, nontransferable bond before it can submit proposals; accepted work earns fees, while fraud proven by a challenge process burns the bond. The bond is tied to a verified contribution history, so one operator cannot cheaply multiply identities: every new persona needs fresh capital and must survive review. A delta in reputation can follow a failed claim, while a cipher-bound audit trail links actions without exposing private data. A hollow identity therefore costs real funds and time, not merely a new account.
